formula: cbind(ballots_cast, active - ballots_cast) ~ 0 + ep + z_share_ba_plus + z_median_age + z_share_moved_past_year + z_share_owner_occupied + (1 | county:party_group) + (1 | county:election_type) + (1 | obs)
formula_notes: ep = interaction(election, party_group, drop = TRUE): a free statewide level for each of the 15 election x party cells present (OTH is absent from the closed primaries).

selection.rule: random-effect variants tried in order; the first non-singular fit with no convergence messages is used
selection.why: The full formula and the one without (1 | county:party_group:election_type) are singular: the county x party x type term is estimated at 0 (it is nearly the same as (1 | obs), with at most three rows per cell and election type), and (1 | county) is estimated at 0 once the covariates are in: the covariates and (1 | county:party_group) take up all county-level variation. Dropping (1 | county) as well leaves the estimates unchanged. zero_sd_terms in each attempt lists the terms at 0.

messages:
Model is nearly unidentifiable: very large eigenvalue
 - Rescale variables?

alpha_draws: Not for use uncalibrated: the alpha draws and the random-effect draws behind s_cp are independent, so alpha + s_cp carries the uncertainty of the population mean (statewide GG22 ballots sd about 42,000), and the parametric bootMer (use.u = FALSE) agrees with that width for the same reason rather than validating it. The forecast calibrates the statewide level per draw and does not use the alpha spread.
